Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate massive, diffuse dilation of the trachea and main bronchi (tracheobronchomegaly) accompanied by multiple large cystic spaces and diverticula, which are pathognomonic features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The "cavities" seen on imaging are actually these markedly dilated airways, and the hilar opacity corresponds to the fluid-filled or mucus-plugged dilated central bronchi characteristic of this condition.
